skill.name: frontend-css
skill.description: Write consistent, maintainable CSS following the project's methodology (Tailwind utility classes) while minimizing custom CSS and adhering to design system tokens. Use this skill when writing or editing CSS files, Tailwind classes in React components (.tsx, .jsx files), when implementing design system colors/spacing/typography, when using Tailwind utility classes, when deciding between framework utilities vs. custom CSS, when optimizing CSS for production with tree-shaking, when configuring Tailwind theme extensions, or when maintaining design consistency across the application.
skill.summary: Guide frontend CSS work toward Tailwind utilities, design tokens, responsive patterns, and production-friendly styling.
skill.author: DevanB

content.value_statement: Frontend teams need consistent CSS that follows project standards. This skill guides Tailwind utilities, design tokens, responsive styling, and production CSS choices.
actual_capabilities: Guides CSS file edits toward the project's frontend styling methodology.
Recommends Tailwind utility classes in React .tsx and .jsx components.
Applies design system tokens for colors, spacing, and typography.
Helps choose framework utilities before adding custom CSS.
Covers Tailwind theme extension decisions using the `@theme` directive.
Highlights responsive breakpoints and production purging or tree-shaking.
limitations: It provides guidance only and does not enforce lint rules by itself.
It depends on the linked project CSS standards being available to the agent.
It does not define a complete Tailwind configuration by itself.
It does not inspect rendered UI unless separate visual tools are used.

use_cases.title: Style React Components
use_cases.description: Apply Tailwind utility classes while keeping component styling aligned with existing project conventions.

use_cases.title: Maintain Design Tokens
use_cases.description: Use approved colors, spacing, and typography choices when implementing or reviewing interface changes.

use_cases.title: Review CSS Consistency
use_cases.description: Identify unnecessary custom CSS and recommend utility-first alternatives before merging frontend changes.

prompt_templates.title: Apply CSS Standards
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single styling task
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the frontend-css skill to style this component with project CSS standards. Prefer Tailwind utilities and design tokens.

prompt_templates.title: Refine Component Styling
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this .tsx component with the frontend-css skill. Replace unnecessary custom CSS with maintainable Tailwind utility classes.

prompt_templates.title: Align a Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the frontend-css skill across this feature. Keep spacing, colors, typography, and responsive behavior consistent with the design system.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Production CSS
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the frontend-css skill to review these styling changes for bundle size, tree-shaking, theme extensions, and framework override risks.

output_examples.input: Style a React settings panel with consistent spacing and responsive behavior.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends Tailwind utilities, design token choices, breakpoint adjustments, and notes where custom CSS is unnecessary.

output_examples.input: Review a frontend change before production release.
output_examples.output: The assistant summarizes style consistency, theme extension impact, responsive coverage, and CSS bundle considerations in plain language.

best_practices: Provide the relevant component files and any design token references.
Ask for Tailwind utility-first changes before requesting custom CSS.
Review responsive states and production CSS impact before accepting changes.
anti_patterns: Using broad custom CSS overrides when a framework utility is available.
Adding colors, spacing, or typography outside the design token system.
Treating the skill as a visual QA tool without rendered UI checks.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps agents write and review frontend CSS using Tailwind utilities and project styling standards.

faq.question: Does it generate complete UI designs?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on CSS methodology, utility classes, tokens, responsiveness, and maintainable styling choices.

faq.question: Can it work with React files?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill explicitly covers Tailwind classes in .tsx and .jsx React components.

faq.question: Does it require Tailwind CSS?
faq.answer: The skill is written for Tailwind and utility-first workflows. It is less useful for unrelated CSS systems.

faq.question: Will it reduce custom CSS automatically?
faq.answer: It can recommend fewer custom rules, but the host agent must still edit and verify the files.

faq.question: Is it safe for production reviews?
faq.answer: It can support production CSS review, but teams should still run their normal tests and visual checks.
